summary: Iteration 14: Owner email (info@chientibike.it) becomes admin on Google sign-in. All 9/9 pytest tests PASS in /app/backend/tests/test_iter14_owner_admin.py in ~2.6s under the default `-n 2 --dist loadscope` xdist config AND under `-n 0`. Covers: (1) POST /api/auth/register with 'info@chientibike.it' (lowercase) → 409 with detail "Per questa email usa \"Continua con Google\"" ✅; (2) POST /api/auth/register with 'INFO@ChientiBike.IT' (mixed case) → 409 (is_owner_email is case-insensitive) ✅; (3) POST /api/auth/register with a random test_iter14_<8hex>@example.com → 200, response.user.role == 'user', token present ✅ (user then deleted by cleanup); (4) POST /api/auth/session with a bogus session_id against the LIVE Emergent backend → 401 with 'Google' in detail ✅; (5) Regression: POST /api/auth/login admin@noleggionuovo.it / Admin2026! → 200 role=admin, token works on GET /api/admin/stats (returns bike_models/active_bookings/total_units/today_bookings/revenue_paid) ✅. GOOGLE-SESSION TESTS use respx to mock https://demobackend.emergentagent.com/auth/v1/env/oauth/session-data while calling /api/auth/session via httpx.ASGITransport against the imported /app/backend/server.py app (in-process, same Mongo); (6) NEW owner Google sign-in → 200, session_token issued, user.role == 'admin' straight from creation; GET /api/auth/me with that token returns role=admin; GET /api/admin/stats with that token returns 200 (admin-gated route works) ✅; (7) PROMOTION path: pre-seed Mongo with {email: info@chientibike.it, role: 'user', password_hash: bcrypt('OldPass123!')}, confirm POST /api/auth/login with OldPass123! returns 200 BEFORE promotion, then mocked Google session → role becomes 'admin'; POST /api/auth/login with OldPass123! afterwards returns 401 (password_hash was $unset) and direct Mongo check confirms the doc has role=admin and NO password_hash key ✅; (8) Non-owner Google email (test_iter14_g_<8hex>@example.com) mocked → 200, user.role == 'user' (owner-only promotion gate holds) ✅; (9) Mocked 401 response from Emergent → /api/auth/session returns 401 ('Sessione Google non valida') ✅. CLEANUP: module-scope autouse fixture deletes every info@chientibike.it doc AND every test_iter14_* doc both before and after the suite; final Mongo state verified empty for both patterns. Shared asyncio loop per module (motor binds to the first loop it sees); respx uses `mock.route(host='testserver').pass_through()` so ASGI calls to the in-process FastAPI app are NOT intercepted while outbound GETs to demobackend.emergentagent.com are. OWNER_ADMIN_EMAILS is set in /app/backend/.env to info@chientibike.it (confirmed). Dependencies: pytest-asyncio==1.4.0, respx==0.23.1 installed via pip (both were missing; now present). Backend running fine on https://bici-disponibili.preview.emergentagent.com. No bugs found.
critical_code_review_comments: server.is_owner_email (server.py:208-212): reads OWNER_ADMIN_EMAILS from env on every call and splits on ',' with .strip().lower() — case-insensitive, supports multiple owners, and lets the main agent toggle the list by just editing .env + restarting. Clean. The input to is_owner_email is expected to be already-lowercased; both callers (register, google_session) do `email = body.email.strip().lower()` or `data['email'].strip().lower()` first, so the invariant holds.

server.register (server.py:216-229): correctly rejects owner emails with 409 and the Italian message before touching Mongo, preventing accidental seeding of an unverified owner account. The order of checks (email format → owner → duplicate) is right. Minor: 409 is a reasonable code for 'can't register this email this way'; some teams would prefer 403, but 409 is defensible and the test contract pins to 409.

server.google_session (server.py:241-265): handles all three cases (new owner, existing non-admin owner, existing admin owner) in one $set/$unset update, and importantly does $unset: {password_hash: ''} ONLY in the promotion branch — an already-admin owner's `password_hash` (if somehow set) is left alone, which is fine because the seeded ADMIN account (admin@noleggionuovo.it) is a different email. The 'name': user.get('name') or data.get('name') clause preserves the user-chosen name if present, otherwise falls back to the Google-provided name — nice UX. One tiny observation: for a BRAND-NEW owner the doc is inserted without a `password_hash` field, which is correct; motor's insert_one is awaited; after insert the code pops '_id' from the local dict defensively (though insert_one doesn't inject _id into the dict in motor 3.x — still, no-op is harmless). Not a bug.
server.google_session also uses user.find_one AFTER the update to re-read the fresh doc for `to_public(user)` — correct because the local `user` dict is stale after $set/$unset. Good discipline.
test_credentials.md (/app/memory): accurately documents the OWNER_ADMIN_EMAILS behaviour and the 409 contract on password sign-up for the owner email. Matches the implementation.

Minor: register's HTTPException for owner emails raises 409 with the Italian message 'Per questa email usa "Continua con Google"'. The English translator in EN_ERRORS does NOT have an entry for this specific key, so an English-speaking client (Accept-Language: en-*) will still see the Italian string. Not critical (the ask was Italian app), but worth adding to EN_ERRORS for consistency with the other translated messages: suggest 'For this email, please use "Continue with Google"'.
DO NOT MODIFY: metro/app.json/babel are protected. backend/.env OWNER_ADMIN_EMAILS=info@chientibike.it is correct and must not be commented or changed.
seed_data_creation: No persistent seed data. Tests create ephemeral docs that are cleaned up: (a) one random test_iter14_<hex>@example.com user from the register-200 test (deleted by in-test cleanup + module-scope autouse teardown); (b) one test_iter14_g_<hex>@example.com from the non-owner Google session test (same cleanup); (c) one info@chientibike.it doc from the new-owner Google session + one from the promotion test (both deleted by module-scope autouse teardown, which uses delete_many on the owner email AND on /^test_iter14_/ regex). Final Mongo state verified: 0 info@chientibike.it docs, 0 test_iter14_* docs. Admin seeded user admin@noleggionuovo.it (role=admin, bcrypt password) is left intact — only READ by the regression test. Real bikes/bookings not touched (no POST /api/bookings, no admin PATCH).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Re-run with EITHER `cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/test_iter14_owner_admin.py` (uses the pytest.ini default `-n 2 --dist loadscope`) OR `python -m pytest tests/test_iter14_owner_admin.py -n 0` for serial. ~2.5s runtime. Dependencies ADDED THIS ITERATION: pytest-asyncio and respx (both via `pip install`); they are NOT in /app/backend/requirements.txt — if the pod is rebuilt from requirements, re-install both before running. The test uses a SHARED module-scope asyncio loop because motor's AsyncIOMotorClient binds to the first event loop it's used in — if you split any Google-session test into its own loop you WILL get 'Event loop is closed' on the second call. respx usage pattern: `with respx.mock(assert_all_called=False) as mock: mock.get(SESSION_URL).mock(return_value=httpx.Response(...)); mock.route(host='testserver').pass_through()` — the pass_through is critical, otherwise the ASGI call via httpx.ASGITransport also gets intercepted and errors with 'not mocked!'. For an ASGI-level test to work, importing server triggers startup events (motor index creation, seed bikes) once per module — don't be surprised to see sheet_sync_loop and reminder_loop background tasks start up. OWNER_ADMIN_EMAILS lives in /app/backend/.env (value: info@chientibike.it); do NOT comment it out. test_credentials.md is authoritative for admin creds (admin@noleggionuovo.it / Admin2026!). SAFETY contract (unchanged across iterations): never POST /api/bookings with payment_method=store, never mark a stripe booking paid in tests, never edit the 4 real bikes in the admin UI (writes go to the user's real Google Sheet).
rca_of_issue: N/A — all specified behaviours work end-to-end. During test authoring I hit two speedbumps and fixed them in-test: (1) using unittest.mock.MagicMock to replace httpx.AsyncClient inside server.py failed with 'object MagicMock can't be used in await' — resolved by switching to respx (library purpose-built for intercepting httpx) with a pass_through for the ASGI host. (2) Creating a fresh asyncio event loop per test (via new_event_loop()+close()) crashed subsequent tests with 'Event loop is closed' because motor's AsyncIOMotorClient (imported in server.py at module load) caches its event loop on first use — resolved by making a module-scope shared_loop fixture and passing it to every mocked test. Also had to lowercase the random-email test input because server lowercases via .strip().lower() before storing. These are test-harness fixes; the backend code under test is correct and unchanged.
